symptom: Diffusion language models cannot be served with standard AR inference machinery. Continuous batching, paged KV, speculative decode, and FlashDecoding all assume one forward pass per token. Diffusion LMs do S full forward passes per generation, with no KV cache reuse across steps.
root_cause: Diffusion LMs generate by iterative denoising: start from a fully masked sequence, run S denoising steps, each a full forward pass over the current sequence. There is no causal mask (the model sees the entire sequence), no KV cache (every step is a fresh full-attention pass), and no incremental decode (the cost per step is the full sequence length, not one token).
workaround: Use a separate serving path for diffusion LMs. SGLang has a dedicated diffusion LM section with --dllm-algorithm flags. Cache the KV for the prompt portion only (the prompt is stable across steps). Batch many independent sequences so a step's flops are shared across the batch. Use fewer denoising steps for faster inference at the cost of quality.
notes: The existing diffusion-lm-denoising-steps flop record covers the arithmetic. This gotcha covers the practical serving consequence: you cannot just plug a diffusion LM into vLLM or llama.cpp and expect it to work. The serving shape is fundamentally different. SGLang is the only major engine with explicit diffusion LM support. The batch-size regime where diffusion wins is at large batch (compute-bound), not at small batch (where AR is memory-bound and diffusion is compute-bound).
name: Diffusion LM serving shape is fundamentally different from AR
